reviewContext.userProblem: In riela/gmail-collect, GmailMailboxCollector.collectScan (Sources/RielaCLI/GmailCollection.swift) uses maxThreads as a per-run cap on listed and processed threads. A 48-hour ART mailbox scan with more than 150 threads and maxThreads 150 stops every other run with failure stage 'budget' and resumes next run, delaying mail by about an hour.
requiredOutcomes: maxThreads means the maximum number of in-flight per-thread reads (version check, full thread read, messageBodyBytes); effective concurrency is min(maxThreads, 16).
One run lists every page until the provider reports no next page, at page size 50 (min(50, 10000 - listed) near the hard limit), and processes every listed thread.

All provider requests in a scan (profile, listing, thread reads) take start slots from one shared GmailCollectionRequestLimiter actor spaced by minRequestIntervalSeconds; the limiter refuses slots not strictly before the deadline and refused requests are not counted in requestCount.

Outcomes are accepted sequentially in queue order on the parent, preserving pending_collection, thread_versions acknowledgement only for accepted threads, deferred/failed rotation via retry_after, output byte reservation, invalidated IDs, mailbox_version freezing and cancellation propagation.
Early stops record real stages 'deadline' (once), 'output-budget' (with threadId), 'listing-limit', 'listing', 'thread', 'requested-body'; the generic 'budget' stage is removed.

Existing resume/rotation tests are rewritten to stop via deadline or output budget and still pass; new tests cover full multi-page listing with maxThreads 1, concurrency bound 4 and clamp 16, in-order results, shared limiter spacing, listing-limit stage and coordinator prefetched profile requestCount.
swift test --filter GmailCollection passes and the full RielaCLITests suite has no new failures.

No change to GmailCollectionOptions validation (maxThreads range 1...10000, default 100) or the scope hash; maxThreads never enters scope identity.
No change to the pending_collection key set, listing.maximum 10000, advancePage, threadSelection, bodySelection, gmailIdentifier or gmailIDSet.
No change to coordinator scope archive, retry backlog, fresh-capacity failure or backlog complete=false behavior.
No README/docs changes (none reference maxThreads), no new dependencies, no commit/push/merge by workers.
constraints: Swift 6 strict concurrency with no @unchecked Sendable, nonisolated(unsafe) or Mutex in production code; macOS 14 deployment target.
fetch closures in scan, coordinator and adapter are @Sendable, as are the injectable clock and wait.
Every swift build/test/swiftlint runs as arch -arm64 /bin/zsh -lc with logs under tmp/gmail-collect-concurrency/<gcc-01|gcc-02>/.
Same working directory on main, no worktrees, no git write operations by workers; fresh read plus pre/post SHA-256 per owned file.
gcc-02 guards GmailMessageBodyCollection.swift, GmailCollectionRetryBacklog.swift, GmailCollectionRequestLimiter.swift and the design doc with a shasum pre/post diff.
Scope-hash golden tests (29b73447..., c4ee206a...) must not be edited or weakened.
designDecisionsAndRationale: Listing stays sequential because each page needs the previous cursor; only the per-thread phase is concurrent (design §'Full listing, concurrent thread reads and early-stop reasons').
Concurrency clamp min(maxThreads, 16) keeps compatibility of the accepted maxThreads range while bounding provider load and look-ahead memory.
Look-ahead window equals the concurrency: a read launches only while fewer than C IDs are launched but unaccepted, bounding wasted work after a stop.
Shared limiter actor reserves the slot before suspending (actor-reentrancy safe) and sleeps only slot - now, so starts are spaced across workers rather than per worker.
Deadline refusal is a dedicated GmailCollectionDeadlineRefusal error so a deadline stop is distinguishable from provider .timeout errors.
A read refused before its first request stays pending (not deferred); a read refused after a request started is deferred and becomes retry_after so a slow item cannot monopolize runs.
Coordinator passes its already-read profile as prefetchedProfile (counted as the first granted slot) instead of capturing a mutable usedProfile flag, keeping spacing and requestCount.
Malformed stored versions are parsed inside the worker's error mapping so they fail only that ID.
intentionalTradeoffs: Throughput is about one request per minRequestIntervalSeconds regardless of concurrency, so single-run completion still depends on the node deadline.
Removing the per-run cap means large mailboxes may now stop on output-budget or deadline instead of budget.
testBudgetStopsBeforeAnotherProviderCallAndCancellationPropagates now asserts stage 'deadline' instead of 'listing' (accepted divergence).
The pre-existing 10,000-item listing hard limit still never completes such a scan; it is now labeled 'listing-limit'.
supportedEdgeCases: Deadline reached mid-listing or mid-thread-phase returns complete=false with stage 'deadline' and a pending_collection resumed exactly next run.
Output-budget refusal defers the oversized ID, stops new launches and still evaluates completed look-ahead outcomes in order.
Out-of-order concurrent completions are accepted in listing/queue order.
Poison/failed items rotate fairly even with maxThreads 1 (attempts a,b,a,b,a,b).
Old-cursor resume, discovery floor and body-intent scope switches keep their existing semantics.
Cancellation from any worker or the parent propagates with no partial result.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Raising throughput beyond the shared minRequestIntervalSeconds spacing.
Completing listings larger than 10,000 items in one scan.
Concurrency in message-bodies mode or other collectors.
Known timing flakes in the full RielaCLITests suite unrelated to the owned files (rerun alone and classify under tmp/gmail-collect-concurrency/gcc-02/rerun-*.log).

acceptanceCriteria: Sources/RielaCLI/GmailCollectionRequestLimiter.swift defines internal struct GmailCollectionDeadlineRefusal: Error, Sendable and actor GmailCollectionRequestLimiter with init(interval:deadline:clock:wait:), recordPrefetchedGrant(), acquire() async throws and grantedCount, exactly as pinned in the plan; no 'unchecked' in the file.

acquire() checks cancellation, computes slot = max(now, lastSlot + interval), refuses slot >= deadline without changing state or waiting, reserves before awaiting wait(slot - now), and never calls wait with a non-positive value.
GmailCollectionRequestLimiterTests covers the 10 situations in the plan table and passes with 0 failures.

With maxThreads=1 and a 3-page listing, one collectScan lists every page with first == 50 and returns all threads with complete=true and no pending_collection.

With maxThreads=4 at most 4 thread reads are in flight (high-water mark >= 2 and <= 4); maxThreads=10000 clamps to <= 16; threads and invalidated are in listing order; request starts honour minRequestIntervalSeconds via the shared limiter with injected clock/wait.

A deadline reached mid-run returns complete=false, failure stage 'deadline' and a pending_collection that the next run resumes exactly; existing resume/rotation tests are rewritten per the plan turn maps and pass.

Failed-item rotation holds (attempts a,b,a,b,a,b at one-read turns); output-budget refusal records {stage: output-budget, threadId}; listing limit records 'listing-limit' after exactly 200 listing calls.
